title: U.S. House · California's 47th District
area: Coastal and central Orange County, including Irvine and surrounding communities. Redrawn under Proposition 50 (approved November 2025).

context.text: Incumbent Dave Min (D) and Republican Jenny Rae Le Roux advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary; Min received 45.4% of the vote and Le Roux 25.0%, ahead of seven other candidates.

candidates.name: Dave Min
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 45.4% of the vote.

priorities.text: Reproductive freedom, citing his authorship of a California constitutional amendment on abortion and contraception access.
Gun violence prevention, citing legislation he passed prohibiting gun shows on state property.
Climate action, citing legislation he authored to end offshore oil drilling.

positions.summary: Says he authored a California ballot proposition adding abortion and contraception access to the state constitution and has a 100% rating from Planned Parenthood.
Says he passed state legislation prohibiting gun shows on state property and has an 'F' rating from the NRA.
Says he authored legislation to end offshore oil drilling and reduce reliance on fossil fuels, and has a 100% rating from the Sierra Club.
Says he voted against cuts to Medicaid and Medicare and that the enhanced ACA premium tax credits and Medicaid and Medicare funding must be restored.
positions.quote: I believe that we must restore the enhanced premium tax credits and also essential funding to Medicaid and Medicare.

positions.summary: Says he has voted against funding for ICE and calls for guardrails on the agency, and says people who have long lived in the U.S. should not be deported, while also stating he believes in strong border security.
positions.quote: We must rein in the lawlessness and lack of accountability at ICE

record.text: Serves on the Joint Economic Committee, the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, and the Committee on Natural Resources for the 2025-2026 term.
As a California state senator, sponsored roughly 28 bills that were enacted, including eight related to protections for domestic-violence survivors, according to his campaign.

candidates.name: Jenny Rae Le Roux
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 25.0% of the vote.

priorities.text: Public safety, citing rising crime rates and reduced sentencing in California as reasons to increase police staffing.
Government transparency and efficiency: "full transparency of where the money is going, who it is going to."

positions.summary: In her 2022 gubernatorial campaign, said she would work to retain and hire new police officers, support pay increases for officers, and stop prison closures.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 campaign website or Ballotpedia survey found; 2026 Fox News interview gives general themes only. Earlier 2022 gubernatorial statements remain from the existing entry.
